pr_body:
Fixes: #18471

AddAuthorizationCore previously assumed that options were already
registered. This isn't the case in 5.0 in Blazor WASM.

We don't want Blazor to register options in the default host because it
prevents options from being linked out.

note: we will have some remaining work for this issue after this change
is merged. The Blazor WASM hosting changes haven't landed in master yet,
so we'll need to update that code to remove options from the host.

issue_context.title: AddAuthorizationCore should call AddOptions
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

`AddAuthorizationCore` depends on options being registered in the service collection. In server-side ASP.NET Core, this is fine because hosting includes it. In Blazor WASM we're now forced to register options (an extra dependency) in the host, even though Blazor itself doesn't use options.
comments: This will have to happen in .NET 5.0 timeframe or we could consider adding it in a patch, as it should be harmless.
Fixing this in 5.0 sounds good. I don't think this meets the bar for a patch, and I'm not sure we want to couple Blazor WASM to a specific patch version.

review_comments: Almost all of the AddXyz methods would potentially need this, but I guess the idea is to just add it to the one Blazor WASM needs for now?

> Almost all of the AddXyz methods would potentially need this

I'm not 100% sure about that. 

99% of server-side ASP.NET's stuff won't work in Blazor WASM - and it doesn't really make sense for someone to try. If we really wanted to be thorough we could add this everywhere, but I'm not sure what the benefits really are.

This is the one thing I'm aware of that has usage in Blazor WASM. This *is* a mainline scenario though, so we care about it working without extra ceremony.
Logging and HttpClientFactory also add it, you're not using either of those?
In Blazor WASM you're almost certainly not using those 😆
This is a primary scenario and it's included in template, it's needs to be mistake-proof.
